messages:
acme_prod_ops: Hey team — on our Dedicated cluster (VPC) we've had a client report that SSE streams cut out after ~180-250 tokens, then the client reconnects and sometimes sees the tail of the previous stream duplicated. At times we also see 403 auth failures from the same client IP for a few seconds after reconnect. Happening only for their on‑prem users behind a corporate proxy. No issues in Hosted. Curious if anyone has seen packet fragmentation / proxy buffering cause this. Repro steps attached below.

maya (Support): Thanks — sorry for the pain. A couple quick questions: 1) Is this consistently reproducible from the customer's network? 2) Do you have the request id / x-request-id for one of the failing streams so we can correlate? 3) Any ingress (nginx/HAProxy) in front of the dedicated instance?

acme_prod_ops: It's reliably reproducible from their corp office but not from home. We do have an example x-request-id: req-0a7f3c2e. Ingress is our onprem NGINX reverse proxy (they host the customer edge) -> internal LB -> dedicated pods. Their proxy team says they don't change payloads.

jordan (Eng-Infra): Noted. Quick hypothesis: corporate proxy or onprem ingress is doing aggressive buffering or MSS clamping is wrong leading to IP fragmentation. For SSE, any intermediary that buffers until a chunk size threshold will break streaming. Also if the proxy closes or sends FIN mid-stream during fragment reassembly you can end up with partial events and orphaned state that the client sees after reconnect.

lee (NetOps): Agree with jordan. Also seen corporate proxies rewrite Transfer-Encoding / chunked headers which can cause the origin to think it's streaming but the proxy waits for a full chunk before forwarding. Two actionable checks: 1) MTU/MSS mismatch across tunnels (e.g., VXLAN overlay, IPsec) — check for fragmentation drops. 2) NGINX buffering directives.

maya (Support): Can you try these repro steps so we can narrow down? 1) From a client behind the corp proxy run: 
```
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://dedicated.acme.example/v1/streams?session=test-123"
```
Look for pauses then abrupt close. 2) On the edge box capture: 
```
tcpdump -s 0 -w sse_capture.pcap host <client_ip> and port 443
```
And 3) on the nginx edge: paste `nginx -T` and the location block for the stream. Key nginx flags: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ""; chunked_transfer_encoding off;` (some proxies need `proxy_pass_request_headers on;`).

acme_prod_ops: Ran the curl — it starts streaming then after ~8–12s we get a `HTTP/2 200` close and curl reports "Connection reset by peer". tcpdump shows repeated TCP segment retransmits followed by a FIN from the proxy IP. Attached pcap shows lots of small TLS records, then a gap, then a FIN. Nginx config excerpt: 
```
location /v1/streams {
  proxy_pass http://internal-lb;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_request_buffering off;
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
}
```
So we already had `proxy_buffering off`.

jordan (Eng-Infra): Good data. Two more angles: 1) MTU / PMTU: if the customer's corp edge is clamping MSS incorrectly (or does not clamp for TCP SYN) you can get IP fragmentation inside tunnels and some middleboxes drop fragments. Suggest checking `ip link` MTU and overlay MTU on both ends. Also run a PMTU probe: 
```
ping -M do -s 1472 <client_ip>  # starts near 1500 - 28
```
If that fails but smaller sizes work, there's a fragmentation window. Another fix is to enable MSS clamping on the edge firewall: 
```
iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```
2) Some corporate proxies do TLS termination then re-establish another TLS session and will buffer until TLS record sizes hit a threshold. Check the proxy vendor docs for "streaming" or "event-stream" passthrough mode.

lee (NetOps): Also check NAT idle timeouts. If the proxy's keepalive timeout < streaming duration, you'll see mid‑stream TCP teardown. For example some corporate NGFWs default to 10s idle TCP timeout for HTTPS. Tools: `ss -tnpi` on the proxy during a test to see connection state and timers.

acme_prod_ops: Interesting — their proxy team just confirmed they have an inline security appliance that inspects TLS and re-bundles traffic, with an idle timeout of 15s. That matches the timing. They can bump it, but we still saw duplicated trailing tokens on reconnect which worries us (billing duplicates).

maya (Support): Duplicated tokens on reconnect are expected if the client reconnects and server replays the remaining tokens; from billing side each response chunk increments token usage meter. Recommended mitigations: 1) Add a short-lived `stream-session-id` header client-side and server logs so you can detect duplicate reconnects and have the server avoid double-billing for the same session id (or the client include last-seen-token-index on reconnect). 2) Implement idempotency for server side meter: only count tokens once per `session-id` + `sequence` window. We'll flag this pattern to billing engineering.

jordan (Eng-Infra): For immediate reproducible test and to rule out server issues, try running a local direct-to-pod curl (bypass NGINX/proxy) to the internal LB DNS: `curl -v -N https://internal-lb.vpc.local/v1/streams?session=test-123` — if this stays stable but the proxied path fails, the culprit is definitely the middlebox.

acme_prod_ops: Direct-to-pod was stable for >5 minutes. So it's definitely the corporate appliance. They increased keepalive to 65s and enabled a streaming passthrough mode — result: streams no longer drop. We still saw one reconnect where the client reported `403` for ~4s after reconnect. Any idea?

lee (NetOps): The 403 gap often comes from a short auth cache TTL on the proxy or a stale session token on the corp appliance. If the proxy re-terminates TLS it may need to revalidate the token with the auth server and if that backends is rate-limited it can return 403/401 temporarily. Check the proxy's auth cache glue and the token validation logs.

maya (Support): For followups, please provide: 1) the x-request-id for the session that had the 403 (we can look for correlated token checks in the control plane logs), 2) the proxy vendor/logs showing TTL changes, and 3) the client's `stream-session-id` if you can add that to the reconnect flow. We'll escalate to billing for duplicate-metering protection and to infra to add guidance in our Dedicated ops runbook.

acme_prod_ops: Thanks — x-request-id for the 403 case: req-0a7f3c2e (same as earlier). Attached a short auth log from the proxy showing token validation with a 429 from their auth server just before the 403. Looks like a cascading rate limit.

ops-bot: Incident note created — INC-2026-042: "Dedicated SSE disconnects caused by corp proxy buffering + auth validation spike". Assigned to eng-infra and netops.

jordan (Eng-Infra): Next steps I'm taking: 1) Add a KB entry under Dedicated > Networking about SSE best-practices (nginx/proxy directives, PMTU/MSS hints, NAT timeouts). 2) Add a small server-side header we can emit on streams: `x-session-guid` so clients can dedupe server events when reconnecting. 3) Work with billing to prototype idempotent token counting for a `stream-session-id`.

maya (Support): Great — please drop the final checklists here when done. For the customer: suggest they (a) request passthrough/streaming mode on their appliance, (b) ensure keepalive > 60s, (c) enable MSS clamping if tunnels overlay reduces MTU, and (d) include a short `stream-session-id` header on client reconnects to help dedupe.

acme_prod_ops: Done — we pushed the proxy config change and verified stability. Will follow up if we see more flaky behavior. Thanks everyone! :tada:
